finding: 32,245 sold_comps rows across four pre-Panini-era years sit on `panini-donruss`, which holds 4-16 catalog rows in those cells (all bccp-product-structure stubs), while `donruss` holds 680-1,455 checklist rows in each.
rulings: THE ERA RULE ALREADY SAYS SO, IN CODE. productSetKeys.ts sets DONRUSS_SPELLING_POLICY = 'panini-era' with PANINI_DONRUSS_FROM_YEAR = 2009, and spellForEra('panini-donruss', 1987) returns 'donruss'. Verified by RUNNING the function, not by reading the table.

THE SOURCE AGREES INDEPENDENTLY. baseballcardpedia has no `1987_Panini_Donruss` page at all; it places Panini America's Donruss era as beginning in 2014 and calls 1986/1987/1989 the Triopoly / Golden Age / Junk Wax eras.

SCOPED TO PRE-2009 AND NOTHING ELSE. The same spellForEra check returns 'panini-donruss' unchanged for 2019/2020/2021, so modern Donruss football and basketball pool rows are correctly keyed and are NOT here — they are acquisitions, not re-keys.

TWO SHAPES, BECAUSE cardId IS NOT ALWAYS A SLUG. 7,263 rows carry a hiq-slug cardId and are RELOCATE; 24,980 carry an opaque vendor cardId, where the setKey lives only in hobbyiqCardId, and are REPOINT.
NO ROW IS UNDECIDED. Unlike the Upper Deck split this needs no card number: the destination is a function of (year, setKey) alone, so all 32,245 rows in scope resolve.
